editorial:
Imagine stepping back in time to 1966 and having Walt Disney himself act as your personal tour guide. You get to see a version of Disneyland that feels fresh and brand new, full of the excitement of early theme park magic. The vibe is warm and welcoming, making you feel like you are walking right beside Walt as he shows off the latest additions. It is not just a list of rides; it is a look at how a creative mind builds a world for families to enjoy together.

What really stands out is how clear and passionate Walt is when talking about his vision. The pacing is relaxed, which is perfect for a documentary, though some might find it a bit slow compared to today's fast movies. It is a goldmine for history buffs and Disney fans who want to see the original charm of New Orleans Square. If you want the best experience, try tracking down a high-quality digital copy or adding the Blu-ray to your physical collection to keep this piece of history forever. It is a great choice for a cozy family movie night.
endingExplained: As the film wraps up, you see a montage of the park during different seasons to show how the magic changes throughout the year. Walt gives a final heartfelt speech about his hopes for the future of the park and the joy it brings to guests. He ends the tour by inviting you to come visit and create your own memories, leaving you with a feeling of wonder and nostalgia.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves Disney history or old theme parks.
